title: Pain Neuroscience Education in Children and Adolescents with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review
authors: Mónica Pico; Carmen Matey-Rodríguez; Ana Domínguez-García; Noemí Yubero; Alejandro Santos-Lozano; Laura Papetti; Emma Rheel
pain_condition_detail: Pediatric chronic primary and secondary pain; included headaches, abdominal pain, cervical pain, and musculoskeletal pain.
context_note: Most included studies were educational/school settings; one university hospital, one neurology clinic, and two online studies; socio-educational context noted.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS mainly as a practice frame: PNE is positioned as a component of multidisciplinary programs with exercise, family involvement, and multidimensional measures. It does not define BPS or operationalize it as coded variables; domains are reviewed as outcomes/interventions rather than a specified causal system.
integration_mechanism_summary: PNE is framed to change pain understanding, fear, coping, and self-efficacy, which may reduce pain-related disability and, when combined with exercise, reactivate inhibitory pain processes. PA is described as reducing anxiety/depression/fear and breaking the fear–avoidance cycle. Family involvement is proposed to reduce overprotective responses. No full triadic causal model is specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS is invoked repeatedly, but the paper does not define it or turn it into coded variables
conceptual_tensions_2: PNE is framed as part of multidisciplinary biopsychosocial care, yet most measured effects are cognitive, emotional, or behavioral
conceptual_tensions_3: Pain intensity is treated as a core outcome, but the paper says PNE may work better on cognitive, emotional, and behavioral aspects
conceptual_tensions_4: Family/caregiver involvement is recommended as important, but only four studies included parents or caregivers
conceptual_tensions_5: Digital, gamified, and VR delivery formats are promising, but their effectiveness and sustained outcomes remain unclear
additional_observations_1: The review excludes procedural, oncological, primary neurological condition, and recurrent acute pain
additional_observations_2: Most included studies were clinical or pilot trials in school/educational settings, one university hospital, one neurology clinic, and two online studies were reported
additional_observations_3: PNE content was based on international PNE guidelines by Butler and Moseley and Louw and Puentedura
additional_observations_4: Online cognitive behavioral therapy was a comparator/control in Web-MAP2 studies
additional_observations_5: Sex/gender is discussed as both biological and sociocultural
additional_observations_6: Family/caregiver involvement is framed as underused but important for sustainable pediatric chronic pain care
synthesis_note: This pediatric PNE review uses BPS mainly as a practice frame for multidisciplinary care. It extracts PNE effects on pain knowledge, self-efficacy, fear/catastrophizing, function, sleep, parental responses, and some biological markers, but rarely specifies how domains interact. Social content is mostly family/school/system context. BPS is invoked to justify comprehensive care, not operationalized as a three-domain model.
coding_rationale: BPS language mainly justifies multidisciplinary care and multidimensional outcomes. Bio/psych are substantive; social is thinner. Pairwise mechanisms appear, but no full triadic causal model.

title: Pain Neuroscience Education in Children and Adolescents with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review
authors: Mónica Pico; Carmen Matey-Rodríguez; Ana Domínguez-García; Noemí Yubero; Alejandro Santos-Lozano; Laura Papetti; Emma Rheel
pain_condition_detail: Pain neuroscience education in children and adolescents with chronic pain
bps_function_set: background framing; intervention rationale; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: BPS label is used to frame multidisciplinary care and justify integration of PNE with exercise and family involvement, but no substantive three-domain integration is developed.
integration_mechanism_summary: Directional relationships proposed: parental involvement improves clinical outcomes; PNE promotes empathetic family responses. No biological-social or triadic integration proposed.
emergent_labels_7: Child and Adolescent Pain Conceptualization Questionnaire
emergent_labels_12: Basic Scale of Insomnia Complaints and Sleep Quality
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS label usage and minimal biological domain development
conceptual_tensions_2: Tension between claimed multidisciplinary approach and limited social domain integration in studies
conceptual_tensions_3: Tension between PNE's cognitive focus and the need for behavioral change translation
additional_observations_1: PNE interventions showed consistent improvements in pain knowledge but modest effects on pain intensity and emotional outcomes
additional_observations_2: Digital and gamified delivery formats showed promise for engagement and scalability
additional_observations_3: Parental involvement was identified as important but understudied in the included literature
additional_observations_4: Small sample sizes and methodological heterogeneity limited evidence certainty
additional_observations_5: Long-term follow-up was limited, affecting assessment of sustained effects
synthesis_note: This review examines PNE effectiveness in pediatric chronic pain, finding consistent gains in pain knowledge but modest effects on pain intensity and emotional outcomes. The BPS label is used to frame multidisciplinary care and justify integration with exercise and family involvement, but substantive three-domain integration is minimal. Biological domain is mentioned but not elaborated; psychological domain is well-developed; social domain is mentioned but understudied. The review demonstrates the gap between BPS rhetoric and substantive integration.
coding_rationale: BPS typology as 'multifactorial' because all three domains are present but psychological domain is elaborated while biological and social are mentioned. Triadic integration scored 'none' because no three-domain mechanism is proposed. Integration between psychological and social domains scored 'directional' based on claims about parental involvement improving outcomes.
